# Pandamonium v1.0.34

Pandamonium now uses MAD MCP Portal through the same generic native MCP client path as every other configured server. This removes an unnecessary client-side reimplementation and fixes the invalid-argument failure that blocked basic Portal inventory questions.

## MAD-842 — Integrations: make MAD MCP Portal tools native and unify connection identity

### Problem

The Portal integration had drifted into Pandamonium-specific catalog synchronization, generated downstream proxy tools, target reconstruction, and completion rules. That duplicated responsibilities already owned by MAD MCP Portal. In the reported inventory request, the model also serialized optional string filters as `null`; local validation labeled the call as denied, never executed it, and gave the model no correction opportunity.

### Implementation

Pandamonium now treats broker-style servers as ordinary native MCP connections. It consumes their standard initialize instructions and tools/list schemas, selects declared tools through the generic MCP index, and forwards the declared tool name and validated arguments without Portal-specific translation. The removed layer includes synchronized Portal service/tool caches, synthetic `portal.read.*` schemas, service/channel/profile reconstruction, relay metadata, Portal-only completion guards, and the obsolete 30-run acceptance harness.

At the generic MCP boundary, optional non-null fields emitted as `null` are treated as omitted, including fields nested in objects and array items. The normalized arguments are the arguments actually executed. Schema failures are reported as invalid arguments rather than permission denials, and a malformed call gets at most one automatic correction round only when the live MCP annotations prove that the tool is read-only.

### Product value and UI visibility

Users can ask the agent what is available in a configured Portal and let the Portal guide discovery, reference lookup, and downstream execution through its own declared tools. Pandamonium retains generic conveniences—connection identity and health, searchable tool selection, exact schemas, authority gates, result threading, and visible traces—without becoming a second Portal. Existing grouped Portal identity presentation remains unchanged.

### Verification

The complete local Python suite passes 5,535 tests with 5 intentional skips. Focused regressions reproduce the screenshot-shaped `portal.find_tools` arguments, prove optional null omission before execution, cover nested array items, verify exact generic MCP forwarding, and enforce one read-only correction round with terminal behavior afterward. Python compilation and diff hygiene pass. Protected PR checks cover the full Python suite, Chromium browser tests, syntax, Compose, secrets, workflow security, dependencies, and container scanning.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

No dependency, environment variable, database migration, credential, Portal server, or downstream provider change is required. Built-in Pandamonium tool validation remains strict and unchanged; null omission applies only at the external MCP boundary. Writes, unknown capabilities, permission failures, and transport failures are not automatically retried. CT103 remains operator-owned and is not installed, restarted, or tested by this release flow; Leo performs the focused installed acceptance through the atomic updater after publication.
